Board guidance before the ExCo met

Priorities.

  • Safety and the five pillars first. The Board will not approve any item that Lars Wagner fails on safety, quality, the A320 ramp or supply, and no Delay Tactics with naked-fine exposure ($48.32B) [AG-0038, AX-0015, A-0331, AG-0053].
  • Keep NGSA on its technology clock. 2030 is the last year of the 2028-2030 launch window. A 2030 launch enters service in 2037, after the 2035 technology-ready year. Across all six columns, NGSA is the one item that adds +22.27 to +45.82 against hold [AG-0063, A-0225, A-0409, AG-0039].
  • Liquidity and the A+/A1 rating: one programme at a time. Peak programme spend must stay within about one year's FCF ($5.2B). NGSA alone, at $35.52B / 7, is about $5.07B a year and passes. NGSA with an overlapping A350 Re-engine is about $6.67B and does not [AX-0022, A-0402, AG-0062, AX-0104, A-0343].
  • Downside discipline across the whole grid row. The bulletin rules out no column, so S1 to S6 all count. No Board item may lose more than $2B against its default in any of them [AX-0007, AG-0029, AG-0033, A-0364].
  • Returns kept fundable. The NGSA plan must leave the 30-50% payout and the EUR 5bn buyback fundable, with no equity raise and no dividend cut. State money is upside and must not be assumed in the case [AG-0058, AG-0059, AG-0034, A-0348].

Expects to see. (1) The grid row of the submitted orders. On the Board's reading, NGSA + A350: hold is +45.82 / +23.37 / +17.28 / +23.37 / +44.96 / +22.51 across S1 to S6. (2) The row with each Board item at its default. For an NGSA launch that is hold + hold (0.00 / -3.30 / -4.99 / -3.30 / -0.86 / -4.16), which gives NGSA an item value of +45.82 / +26.67 / +22.27 / +26.67 / +45.82 / +26.67. (3) The CEO's expected Boeing scenario and the worst plausible column, which is S3 (fps 7-yr) for the NGSA plan. (4) Toepfer's peak-cash arithmetic, year by year for 2030-2037. It should state which NGSA bill it uses. dashboard_game.md section 2 gives $35.52B, about $5.07B a year, roughly $0.13B under $5.2B. The Board's own card used $30.07B, about $4.3B a year. It should also show any overlap and strain ($0.6B a year), and confirm that the payout and the buyback stay fundable. (5) Wagner's results on safety, quality, the A320 ramp, supply and engineering capacity, including whether he passes any A350 Re-engine in this first round. (6) Any override of a CFO or Wagner test, with its margin over the best passing option in the expected column and in the worst plausible column. (7) The NGSA engine code and the reason for it. (8) A public statement that gives windows, not dates, and never mentions Delay Tactics. (9) If Delay Tactics are proposed at all, the CEO's recorded decision to set aside the team's stricter condition. Any piece that is missing the Board will compute from the brief and note, but a missing piece alone will not be a veto ground.

Would approve.

  • NGSA: launch in 2030 (EIS 2037), with any NGSA engine code; 5, 6 or 7 recommended. Its item value against hold is +45.82 (S1), +26.67 (S2), +22.27 (S3), +26.67 (S4), +45.82 (S5) and +26.67 (S6), so it gains in every column. Peak spend is about $5.07B a year, within $5.2B. EIS 2037 is after the 2035 technology-ready year. It needs a Qualified Majority (ten of twelve present), and on these numbers the Board would give it.
  • A350 Re-engine: hold and Delay Tactics: none. These are the defaults and are never vetoed.
  • A350 Re-engine: launch only in a plan with NGSA: hold, and the Board would not recommend that plan. The A350 Re-engine's item value would be +3.26 (S1), +3.25 (S2-S4) and -0.64 (S5-S6), within the $2B limit, at $1.0B a year. Approval would require the CEO's expected scenario to be S1-S4 and Wagner to pass it on ramp and capacity. The Board would still press for NGSA in its window.

Would veto.

  • A350 Re-engine: launch alongside NGSA: launch. Its item value against NGSA alone is +1.75 (S1), +1.74 (S2), +1.75 (S3), +1.74 (S4), -2.15 (S5) and -2.15 (S6), so it fails the Downside test in two plausible columns. Peak spend would be about $5.07B + $1.0B + $0.6B strain, roughly $6.67B against $5.2B (balance sheet). It would mean two launches in one round, with five overlap years from 2030 to 2035 and $3B of strain (two fronts). Under the plan-level rule the Board vetoes the A350 Re-engine, never NGSA. Acceptable alternative: hold.
  • Delay Tactics: bottleneck or both, in any round. Ground: integrity and abnormal risk. Acceptable alternative: none.
  • Delay Tactics: poaching this round. No Boeing fps is on the public record, so the move would be naked. On the NGSA plan one move is worth -15.74 in S1 and S5 (-15.76 with the A350 Re-engine), driven by the $48.32B fine. That fails both the Downside and the Integrity tests. Acceptable alternative: none.
  • Any override of Wagner's safety, quality, A320-ramp or supply tests. Also any override that adds the A350 Re-engine: in S1-S4 it clears $1B (+1.75), but on a Qualified Majority item it trails NGSA alone by $2.15B in the worst plausible columns, S5 and S6.
  • A350 Re-engine: launch with NGSA held if the CEO's expected scenario is S5 or S6, where it is worth -0.64 in the expected column.

Recommendations.

  • Launch NGSA this round. 2030 is the last year of the 2028-2030 window, and a 2030 launch enters service in 2037, after the 2035 technology-ready year. On the grid it is the robust item: +45.82 / +26.67 / +22.27 / +26.67 / +45.82 / +26.67 against hold in S1 to S6. The Board cannot originate the order. If the ExCo holds NGSA, the rationale should explain why the window is given up. As a Qualified Majority item, the case must carry the finance and industrial directors.
  • One programme at a time: the A350 stays on hold this round. NGSA with the A350 Re-engine fails three Board tests: peak spend of about $6.67B against $5.2B; two launches in one round with five overlap years and $3B of strain; and an item value of -2.15 in S5 and S6. The Board will not accept an override to add it, because on a Qualified Majority item it trails NGSA alone in the worst plausible column.
  • Keep the A350 Re-engine in reserve until NGSA development spend rolls off. On the dashboard's bills, any year with both programmes in development breaks the $5.2B line. Do not launch it once Boeing has launched a 787 Re-engine. When it returns, bring a staged widebody case that shows the 787 Re-engine column.
  • Delay Tactics: none. No fps is on the public record, so any move would be naked. One move costs $15.74B in S1 and S5 on the NGSA plan. Bottleneck and both are integrity vetoes in any round. Poaching could come only after Boeing's fps launch is public, at most once, with NGSA in development, at least $1B ahead of the same plan without it in the expected column, and with the CEO's recorded decision to set aside the team's stricter condition.
  • Peak-cash memo. The CFO should set out annual programme spend for 2030-2037, say which NGSA bill he uses ($35.52B from dashboard_game.md, about $5.07B a year, about $0.13B of headroom to $5.2B), and confirm that net cash still carries the 30-50% payout and the EUR 5bn buyback with no equity raise or dividend cut. State support, such as refundable advances, is upside only and must not be assumed in the case.
  • Engine supply. The NGSA code should keep CFM plus a second maker (5, 6 or 7), as the operating head recommends. Code 7 can never fall into a barred pair with Boeing's fps code. The code can be changed until entry into service, so revisit it in 2035 once engine programmes are public. The code is not a veto ground.
  • Safety and ramp. Wagner's memo should confirm that an NGSA launch in 2030 does not compromise A320 quality, the ramp or supply, and should say whether he passes any A350 Re-engine in this first round. The Board accepts no override of these tests.
  • Public statement: give windows, not dates (entry into service 'in the second half of the 2030s'), lead with safety and the five pillars, and never mention Delay Tactics.

Guillaume Faury frames the round

Question. Do we launch NGSA now, in 2030, the last year of its 2028-2030 window, as our only programme this round (entry into service 2037, after the 2035 technology-ready year), with the A350 held and no Delay Tactics? And can we take that single item to the Board with a peak-cash, downside and production case that holds in all six Boeing columns?

Situation. Round 1, decision year 2030. Public record: - No one has launched anything. Boeing flies the 737 MAX and 787. The engine makers are on LEAP, GTF, GEnx and Trent. - Observed shares for 2026-2029 are the status quo: Airbus 60% of narrowbody, 41.2% of widebody. - The brief reports no safety, quality or supply problem and no inject. Our objective ("Defend the 60/40 edge; protect the A320 family") is met on the hold path, with a worst year of 60.0%. The hold path is not safe, though. Do Nothing scores 0.00 only if Boeing also holds. If Boeing moves (S2-S6) it scores -0.86 to -4.99. 2030 is the last year of the NGSA window. Launched now, NGSA enters service in 2037, consistent with "around 2037" and "the second half of the next decade" [A-0409, AX-0020, dashboard_game section 5]. We do not know Boeing's intentions. The grid's S1-S6 are its plausible orders, and the bulletin rules none out. - My provisional expectation is S2: an fps launched on a 10-year ramp, entering service in 2040. Boeing ties a new aircraft to repairing its balance sheet and to "not before 2035" (profile section 7, a prior and not a script). I will confirm the scenario at decide. - The worst plausible column for an NGSA plan is S3: fps on a 7-year ramp, entering service in 2037, the same year as NGSA. - A 737 Rate Increase (2030-only order) is not one of the six columns. Our reaction to it is no programme change (profile section 5, row 7). No Boeing fps is on the public record, so any Delay Tactics would be naked and would draw the $48.32B fine. The Board's guidance (risk aversion 4 of 5, horizon 4 of 5) asks for: - NGSA now, and one programme only; - peak programme spend inside about $5.2B a year; - no Board item losing more than $2B against its default in any of S1-S6; - payout and buyback kept fundable; - no Delay Tactics. Objective outlook, for the record. Against any fps launch, the 60/40 edge cannot hold in the long run on this board: - S2 and S4: a three-year lead, after which share settles toward about 53% Airbus; - S3: the same entry year, converging to 50/50; - S1 and S5: NGSA alone, gaining 3 pp a year, so the objective is met. The GM scores the objective; it never changes the payoff. I will not trade PV for it unless I size and state a premium.

Options to test.

  • A. NGSA launch + A350 hold + Delay Tactics none. This is my lean and the company default for 2030. - Grid, S1 to S6: +45.82 / +23.37 / +17.28 / +23.37 / +44.96 / +22.51. - NGSA's item value against hold: +45.82 / +26.67 / +22.27 / +26.67 / +45.82 / +26.67. It gains in every column. - The worst column (S3, +17.28) stays positive. - Engine code 5, 6 or 7, as Wagner recommends.
  • B. NGSA hold + A350 hold + Delay Tactics none. This is the order default and the Board's reference row. - Grid: 0.00 / -3.30 / -4.99 / -3.30 / -0.86 / -4.16. - It gives up the window and is negative in five of six columns. - It is only the benchmark for A's item value.
  • C. NGSA + A350 Re-engine. I will test it but expect to strike it. - Grid: +47.57 / +25.11 / +19.03 / +25.11 / +42.81 / +20.36. - Against A: +1.75 / +1.74 / +1.75 / +1.74 / -2.15 / -2.15. - It means two launches in one round (rule 6) and five overlap years with $3B of strain. - Peak spend is about $6.67B a year against the $5.2B line. - It fails the Board's $2B downside test in S5 and S6, and the Board would veto it. - No override is available: rule 6 is a company red line, and the Board rejects any override that adds the A350 Re-engine.
  • D. NGSA hold + A350 Re-engine. Reference only. - Grid: +3.26 / -0.05 / -1.74 / -0.05 / -1.50 / -4.80. - It gives up the NGSA window for a derivative and trails A by $19.0B to $46.5B in every column. - The Board would not recommend it.
  • E. Delay Tactics rows. I will strike them on red lines and list them only so the Board record shows the arithmetic. - One move on the NGSA plan, against A: -15.74 in S1 and S5 (the naked fine); +1.57 in S2, S4 and S6; +2.05 in S3. - Both moves: -16.25 in S1 and S5 against A. - No fps is on the public record, so rule 4 bars any move. - Bottleneck and both are integrity vetoes in any round. - The Board vetoes poaching this round.
  • F. Engine-code sub-test on supply certainty only, since the code does not change our payoff: - 5 (Rolls-Royce + CFM); - 6 (Pratt & Whitney + CFM, today's A320neo dual-source pairing [A-0243]); - 7 (all three; never in a barred pair; an unready maker is dropped, so CFM always backstops it).

Red lines.

  • The five pillars (safety, quality, integrity, compliance, security). Every order and every public word must stand on them. They are never overridden and never traded for PV [AX-0073, AX-0081].
  • Rule 1, the NGSA clock. No entry into service before the 2035 technology-ready year. The launch window is 2028-2030, so 2030 is the last launch year, giving entry into service in 2037 [AX-0020, AX-0006, A-0409].
  • Rules 2 and 7, our own clock. Whatever Boeing chooses (fps on a 7-year ramp, a 10-year ramp or via Embraer, or nothing), NGSA moves neither earlier nor later, and it is never cancelled in reaction to Boeing.
  • Rule 6, one new launch this round. NGSA and the A350 Re-engine together are deleted. The overlap limit of 2 years or less (unless the grid shows at least $1B more) also fails: the A350 Re-engine adds -2.15 in S5 and S6 [A-0343, A-0401].
  • Rule 3, no A350 Re-engine after a 787 Re-engine. It is not binding yet, because no 787 Re-engine is on the record. It governs round 2 onward if S5 or S6 materialises.
  • Rules 4 and 5, plus the team's stricter condition: no Delay Tactics this round. - No fps is on the public record, so any move would be naked (the $48.32B fine). - Bottleneck and both are integrity vetoes in any round. - Poaching becomes possible only after Boeing's fps is public, while NGSA is in development, with at least $1B on the grid, and only with my recorded decision to set aside the team's condition that the move must change who enters service first. - The default is off, and it is never named in public [A-0299, A-0474, A-0331].
  • The Board's would-veto list, carried into this round: - an A350 Re-engine launched alongside NGSA (peak spend about $6.67B against $5.2B; -2.15 in S5 and S6; two launches); - Delay Tactics bottleneck or both, in any round; - Delay Tactics poaching this round; - any override of Wagner's safety, quality, A320-ramp or supply tests; - any override that adds the A350 Re-engine; - an A350 Re-engine with NGSA held if my expected scenario is S5 or S6.
  • The Board's own tests: - peak programme spend at or under about $5.2B a year, one year's FCF (EUR 4.75bn at an assumed $1.10 per euro) [AX-0104]; - no Board item losing more than $2B against its default in any of S1-S6; - the 30-50% payout and the EUR 5bn buyback stay fundable, with no equity raise and no dividend cut; - state support is upside only and is not assumed in the case [AX-0022, AG-0062].
  • Override budget: at most one per game. An override needs at least $1B over the best passing option and is recorded as a Board item. It is never used against the five pillars or a company red line, and never against Wagner's safety, quality, ramp or supply results. None is planned this round.

Initial lean. Objective. The briefing goal is "Defend the 60/40 edge; protect the A320 family". The GM scores it; it does not change the payoff, and I trade no PV for it. On plan A, by column: - S1 and S5: NGSA alone gains 3 pp a year from 2037 (cap 80%). Any of the following triggers a re-phasing inside the programme, never an acceleration: a forecast overrun above $0.88B; a peak year more than 2.5% above the average; or the euro below about $1.07. Any breach comes back to the Board as an item [AX-0104, AX-0008].

Board guidance before the ExCo met

Priorities.

  • Safety and readiness come first. We accept no date without test evidence and no launch with an unresolved safety or durability flag. A 2030 Ducted is ready in 2036, one year ahead of the earliest new narrowbody entry (2037 for an NGSA or a 7-year fps; 2040 for a 10-year fps). No Open Fan date before 2045 [CG-0009, CG-0018, CX-0009, CX-0012, CX-0658].
  • Keep every new narrowbody on a CFM engine, but only where the grid pays for it. Do Nothing costs $32.07B to $105.01B in every column where an airframer launches (S2 to S6). A Ducted recovers $8.43B to $13.05B of that in S2 to S5. It loses no more than its own bill ($4B, or $6B with the strain), and the full bill is lost only if the rivals hold (S1) [CG-0017, CX-0609, CX-0564, CX-0493].
  • Keep RISE whole as technology, and make it a product only on an airframer path. Any narrowbody launched this round enters service in 2037 to 2040, before a 2045 Open Fan. So a 2030 Open Fan waits, and its item value is -$15.67B to -$57.59B in S2 to S6 against an $8B bill. No Open Fan or Lobby this round, and the one RISE allowance stays unused [CX-0469, CX-0205, CX-0147, CX-0174, CG-0065].
  • Keep the balance sheet and the payout intact: the A-range rating and at least 70% of free cash flow returned. The largest package that passes (Ducted + Partner Embraer + GEnx upgrade) commits about $1.0B a year against about $2.5B of room. Take on a second project only where the grid pays the $2B strain [CG-0022, CX-0645, CG-0063, CG-0002, CG-0064].
  • State the Safran gate for every CFM item, with the reason the partner would agree. A defence that keeps an airframer on CFM, or serving every airframer, fits joint practice. A Ducted with no defensive trigger does not [CX-0184, CG-0065, CG-0066, CX-0587].

(2) For each Board item: the submitted row and the row with that item at its default, in every column, with the expected and the worst column named. Partner Embraer defaults with the Ducted because it needs a CFM engine. Our reading of the grid: the best plan is GEnx upgrade in S1 (+0.78) and S6 (-104.23), and Ducted + Partner Embraer + GEnx upgrade in S2-S5 (-20.69 / -71.86 / -50.10 / -48.96). (3) Ghai's tests with numbers: price/cost positive; R&D and strain per year against 2-3% of revenue (about $0.9-1.3B on $44B) and against the roughly $2.5B left after a 70% payout of about $8.5B 2028 free cash flow; any rating effect, if his memo shows one. Would approve.

  • ducted engine: launch when your expected column is S2, S3, S4 or S5. Item value alone is +10.17 / +10.17 / +8.43 / +10.88. Recommendations.

  • Show each Board item against Do Nothing in your expected column and in the worst column, with the column weights in predictions. For the Ducted the worst column is S1 (-$4.00B alone, -$6.00B in the package), with S6 next (-$0.49B, -$1.38B). We decide on the grid, not the narrative.
  • If you launch the Ducted, launch it now as a defence and say so. Ready in 2036, it is in place before any new narrowbody launched this round enters service (2037 at the earliest). A 2035 launch would be ready only in 2041, after a 2030 NGSA's 2037 entry. Have Ali confirm the 2036 date on test evidence, and resolve any safety or durability flag cross-functionally.
  • Address Culp's 20% fuel-burn red line for a Ducted in the rationale. Ali's own view is that a ducted engine gets less than half the fuel-burn gain. Strike it or rebut it, for example by showing it is a defensive engine with RISE still the next generation and durability not traded. Otherwise we will treat it as an unresolved red-line flag.
  • Keep RISE whole as technology rather than a 2030 product: no Open Fan or Lobby this round, and keep the one RISE allowance for an airframer path. Say plainly what follows. If a new narrowbody is launched this round, any Open Fan will wait for 2045. Then the 'Introduce the Open Fan' objective, which needs a launch by 2035, may have to be given up on the dashboard. We will not stretch the airframer-path test to meet it.
  • Add a second project only where the grid pays the $2B strain. GEnx upgrade works alone (+$0.78B) or together with both Ducted and Partner Embraer (+$0.78B). Never put it beside a Ducted alone (-$1.22B). Partner Embraer pays only with a Ducted, and not if rivals hold.
  • State the Safran gate for each CFM item and why the partner would agree. The Ducted is a defence that keeps an airframer on CFM. Partner Embraer serves every airframer and is offered without locking Boeing or Airbus out.
  • Keep the payout whole. State the R&D and strain per year: $0.67B for the Ducted, $1.0B for the three-item package. Set that against about $2.5B of room after returning at least 70% of the roughly $8.5B 2028 free cash flow. Put every premium in dollars in premium.
  • Public statement: name no rival, blame no one, give no Open Fan entry before 2045 and no CFM price talk without Safran. Tell the market what we know and what we don't.

Larry Culp frames the round

Question. What game are we playing, and how do we win? [CX-0467, CX-0319] The game is the installed base on the next narrowbody, not share for its own sake [CX-0422, CX-0493]. Whatever airframe launches this round enters service in 2037 (NGSA, or fps on a 7-year ramp) or 2040 (fps on a 10-year ramp or via Embraer), and its engines pay us in shop visits well into the 2050s. "We don't have a birthright on that next order." [CX-0564] We win by being on every new airframe that launches, with an engine ready before that airframe enters service. We do it without pressing any airframer into an Open Fan wait [CX-0205], without calling a ducted engine our next generation, and without risking the balance sheet or the payout. One call decides this round. Do we believe nobody moves (S1)? Or do we plan for an airframer launch where we may not be selected (S2-S6)? Everything else follows from the grid, and we get paid in dollars, not in percentages [CX-0630].

Situation. PUBLIC RECORD, 2030: no programme has launched. Everyone flies today's products (737 MAX, 787, A320neo, A350; LEAP, GTF, GEnx, Trent). Shares held flat from 2026 to 2029: NB airframes Boeing 40% / Airbus 60%; NB engines CFM 76% / P&W 24% / RR 0%; WB engines GEnx 42% / Trent 58%. No rival NB engine is launched, committed or selected on the record. No Joint Venture commitment is on it either. OUR POSITION: ΔPV +0.00 and yield 100.0% (EV $160B). Objective: NB dominance is met today (76%; the test is at least 50% in 2040, 2045 and 2050). Introduce the Open Fan is not met (not launched). For an Open Fan to be ready by 2050 it must launch by the 2035 round (launch + 10, and not before 2045). OPEN SLOTS: both new narrowbodies (NGSA, fps) and both widebody Re-engines are unlaunched. Today the A320neo is dual-sourced and the 737 is ours alone. WHAT THE GRID SAYS: Do Nothing costs $32.07B (S2) to $105.01B (S6) in every column where an airframer launches. A rival selection takes our slot in S3 (an NGSA on code 2 takes Airbus's whole slot) and S6 (codes 1 and 2 take both). In S2, S4 and S5 we share the slot. The best plan in S1 and S6 is GEnx upgrade (+0.78 / -104.23). The best plan in S2-S5 is Ducted + Partner Embraer + GEnx upgrade (-20.69 / -71.86 / -50.10 / -48.96). The decision is the same in all four launch columns. It turns only on how much weight S1 carries. HARD RULE 3 (H3) TRIGGER: not met on the public record. It is met on the grid, because S3 and S6 show a rival selection taking our slot. TIMING: a Ducted launched in 2030 is ready in 2036, one year before the earliest new-NB entry (2037). A Ducted launched in 2035 would be ready only in 2041. OPEN FAN: launched now, it is ready in 2045 at the earliest. Every NB launched this round enters service in 2037-2040, before that, so the wait penalty applies (35 pp of NB share, or 20 pp with lobbying). A 2035 launch is ready in 2045 just the same. OBJECTIVE, my reading of the public rules (inference; the brief gives no share path by column): the 50% NB line is at risk from 2040 in S3 and S6, and possibly in S4-S5. The only levers that push toward it are Ducted (+10 pp) and Embraer (+5 pp). BOARD GUIDANCE (non-binding; its veto comes after my decision). It WOULD VETO: - Open Fan in any combination. Its item value is -8.00 (S1) to -57.60 (S2), and its RISE premium is above $15B in five of six columns. - Lobby without a live Open Fan. - GEnx as the second project beside a Ducted alone (-1.22 to -1.23, which is the strain). - Partner Embraer with S1 expected, with S6 expected and no GEnx, or without an approved Ducted. - A Ducted in any of these cases: S1 or S6 expected with no H3 trigger named; weights that push its weighted item value below zero; a ready year before 2036; an Ali safety or durability flag left unresolved; or my 20% fuel-burn line left unresolved. A Ducted framed as product strategy fails the CFM parity rule (Safran consent). - Any premium above $2.0B this round. It WOULD APPROVE: - A Ducted with S2-S5 expected, or under H3 (trigger S3) if its weighted value over the six columns is at least zero (equal weights: +5.86 alone, +6.55 in the package). - GEnx alone, or as the third project. - Partner Embraer with an approved Ducted in S2-S5. - Packages within about $1.0B a year against about $2.5B of room. It asks for: the expected column and weights; every item against its default in every column; Ghai's tests with numbers; Ali's ready years and any flags; the Safran gate per item; and a public statement that names no rival, blames no one, gives no Open Fan entry before 2045 and contains no CFM price talk.

H2 bars it, the RISE allowance would run past $15B in five columns, and a 2030 launch is ready no earlier than a 2035 one.

Red lines.

  • Safety, quality, delivery and cost, always in that order [CX-0658]. No launch carries an unresolved safety or durability flag, and safety calls are made cross-functionally [CX-0012].
  • H1: never refuse an airframer, never lock one out. We offer every engine to both airframers and to Embraer; the LEAP derivative is an offer, not a refusal [CX-0587, CX-0185].
  • H2: never press an airframer into the Open Fan wait. Every NB launched this round enters service in 2037-2040, before a 2045 Open Fan, so no Open Fan this round unless it is declared as the one RISE allowance. I do not intend to declare it [CX-0205, CX-0469].
  • H3: a Ducted only as a defence, never as our next generation. The trigger I name is on the grid: S3 (a code-2 NGSA takes Airbus's slot) and S6 (codes 1 and 2). Nothing is on the public record yet [CX-0564; CX-0183].
  • H5: never cancel RISE for cost while an airframer may want it. RISE stays whole as technology, with no program dividend [CX-0174, CX-0398].
  • H6 (through Ali): no date without test evidence. Ducted 2036; no Open Fan before 2045 [CX-0009, CX-0008].
  • H7: the Safran gate on every CFM NB order (Ducted, Open Fan, Embraer, Lobby). GEnx is GE alone. No CFM price talk without Safran [CX-0184, CX-0166].
  • H8: no public blame and no comment on rivals [CX-0625, CX-0580].
  • H9: doctrine plus objective premium at most $2.0B this round and $4.0B in the game. The one RISE allowance is capped at $15B and must be declared in full against the best non-RISE plan.
  • My 20% line: a next-generation engine needs at least 20% better fuel burn [CX-0217]. It binds RISE as the next generation. It does not bar a defensive Ducted under H3, which is never offered or described as the next generation (inference).
  • Durability is not traded for fuel burn [CX-0208]. This binds the Ducted too, so Ali must confirm it.

Initial lean. LEAN (to be tested, not decided): - ducted engine: launch, now, as a defence under H3. The trigger is the grid: S3 and S6 show a rival selection taking our slot. It is ready in 2036, one year ahead of a 2037 entry. Earlier is better, because a 2035 launch would be ready only in 2041. - Embraer partnership: launch, with the Ducted. - GEnx: GEnx upgrade, as the third project, never as the second beside a Ducted alone. - Open Fan: hold. - emissions lobbying: hold. RISE stays whole as technology, and the one RISE allowance stays unused this round [CX-0469, CX-0214]. EXPECTED COLUMN: - Central read: S2. On the public rules Airbus has the strongest pull to launch this round (an NGSA alone gains 3 pp a year), and today's A320neo is dual-sourced. - Low case, read as hard: S3. We have no birthright [CX-0564]. - S1 is where the record stands today. - Initial weights: S1 0.25, S2 0.30, S3 0.15, S4 0.05, S5 0.15, S6 0.10. - The package is the best grid plan in S2-S5, so the premium is $0. - Weighted: package -38.70 against hold -45.41 and GEnx alone -44.64. The S2 row is -20.69. I will book expected PV low, at the weighted figure or below, not at S2 [CX-0248, CX-0536]. SAFRAN GATE: - Ducted: a defence that keeps an airframer on CFM. It fits joint practice in serving both airframers, so consent is assumed once the H3 trigger is stated [CX-0185, CX-0587]. - Partner Embraer: a CFM engine for a third airframer. It serves every airframer and locks nobody out, so consent is assumed (inference; there is no Embraer evidence). - Open Fan and Lobby: held, so there is nothing to gate. RISE stays 50-50 technology [CX-0166]. - GEnx: GE alone, no gate. - No CFM price talk without Safran [CX-0184]. OBJECTIVE: - The Ducted and Embraer are the only levers that push NB share toward 50% in S3-S6, and they pay on the grid, so no premium is spent. - If an NB launches this round, a 2035 Open Fan waits too, and the 'introduce' goal may have to be given up. I won't stretch the airframer test to meet it. WHAT CHANGES MY MIND: - Test evidence that doesn't back 2036, or a safety or durability flag we can't close: then the Ducted is held. - Supply that can't carry three projects: then the Ducted goes alone. - Ghai showing the S1 weight should be above about 0.6: then GEnx alone. PUBLIC STATEMENT PLAN: tell you what we know and what we don't [CX-0436]; name no rival; give no Open Fan entry before 2045. It's that simple, ain't that hard.

Track record: my demonstration-type dates slipped (the RISE fly demo moved from mid-decade to 'this decade'; the LEAP-1B kit ran about a year late), so a 1-year margin is thin. A 1-year slip still meets 2037, and a longer slip still earns from its ready year.

Open Fan + Lobby + GEnx against GEnx alone: -11.00 / -39.34 / -35.05 / -35.87 / -40.75 / -18.01. Culp's lean holds the Open Fan, so his plan does not fail this test. Ask (2), RISE status: real testing is under way [CX-0013, CX-0216, CX-0222]. The evidence shows no open durability failure, but it ends in October 2025. The ground and flight test is set for 'this decade' and is not yet reported [CX-0211].
Physics: the 20% line and the Ducted's wordingCall RISE the next generation only at 20% or better. So the Ducted will not meet 20%. The 20% red line binds RISE as the next generation. For the Ducted it is answered by the defensive framing, not struck. I recheck the statement's wording at step 4.
Durability firstNo plan trades durability or time on wing for fuel burn or schedule. The rule I hold: durability holds the date, not the reverse. If testing shows 2036 needs a durability shortcut, the date moves and I report it as a flag. Larry Culp decides

Orders. Launch ducted engine; Partner with Embraer; GEnx upgrade

Rationale. WHAT GAME, HOW WE WIN [CX-0467]. The game is the installed base on the next narrowbody, not share for its own sake [CX-0422, CX-0493]. Do Nothing costs $32.07B (S2) to $105.01B (S6) in every column where an airframer launches. A new NB launched this round enters service in 2037-2040. We have no birthright on that order [CX-0564]. We win by having a new CFM engine ready before that entry, offered to every airframer. We don't press anyone into an Open Fan wait, and we keep the payout whole. DECISION: ducted launch, Embraer partnership launch, genx GEnx upgrade, Open Fan hold, emissions lobbying hold. This is the best grid plan in S2-S5 (-5.22 / -20.69 / -71.86 / -50.10 / -48.96 / -105.61, S1-S6). Against hold it runs -5.22 / +11.38 / +13.82 / +10.94 / +13.62 / -0.60. Both Ghai and Ali recommend the same orders. EXPECTED COLUMN: S2. Airbus has the strongest pull on the public rules (an NGSA alone gains 3 pp a year), and code 6 repeats today's dual-sourced A320neo, which is the record, not a hope. The low-case column is S3, and the decision is the same there. Weights are in predictions: S1 0.25, S2 0.30, S3 0.15, S4 0.05, S5 0.15, S6 0.10. I book expected PV at the equal-weight -50.41, below the -38.70 on my weights and well below S2's -20.69 [CX-0248, CX-0536]. EACH BOARD ITEM AGAINST ITS DEFAULT (S1-S6): - Ducted. Embraer defaults with it, so the default row is GEnx upgrade alone. -6.00 / +10.61 / +13.05 / +10.17 / +12.85 / -1.38. Expected S2: +10.61. Worst S1: -6.00, exactly its bill ($4B R&D + $2B strain). Weighted +5.94 on my weights, +6.55 equal; breakeven at an S1 weight of 0.62. Alone against hold: -4.00 / +10.17 / +10.17 / +8.43 / +10.88 / -0.49; weighted +5.58 / +5.86. - Partner Embraer. Default row is Ducted + GEnx upgrade. 0.00 / +2.44 / +4.88 / +3.73 / +3.97 / +1.12. Expected +2.44, worst 0.00; never negative. - GEnx upgrade. Default row is Ducted + Embraer. +0.78 / +0.78 / +0.78 / +0.77 / +0.77 / +0.78. It runs as the third project, not the second. HARD RULE 3 TRIGGER (named): S3, where an NGSA on code 2 takes Airbus's whole slot from CFM; also S6 (codes 1 and 2). It is on the grid, not yet on the public record. Ghai passes the Ducted's volumes-first test under this carve-out (+10.17 alone, +13.05 in the package in S3). THE S1 COST, NAMED [CX-0301, CX-0609]. If nobody moves, the package costs $6.00B against GEnx alone ($5.22B against hold), and the Ducted alone costs $4.00B. That is the whole bill, buying nothing. It is worth it for four reasons: - Every launch column costs $32-105B under Do Nothing, and the package recovers $10-13B in each of S2-S5. - The downside is bounded at the bill. - The weighted value is positive unless S1 carries more than about 62%. - Timing is now or never for this round's airframes: a 2030 launch is ready in 2036, one year ahead of a 2037 entry, while a 2035 launch is ready only in 2041. A late Ducted still earns from its ready year, but S3 is the slot where being late costs most. TIE-BREAK. The package and Ducted + Embraer are 0.77-0.78 apart in every column, within epsilon. Safety and quality do not separate them: Ali raises no flag, and the GEnx upgrade is a derivative on a proven lineage. Delivery and cost favour the package: it defends the 787 customer on product [CX-0599, CX-0615] at +0.78 with no added strain. Ghai also vetoes Ducted + Embraer without GEnx. The package beats Ducted alone by more than epsilon in S2-S5 (+1.21 to +3.65). OPEN FAN AND LOBBY: HOLD. H2 applies: every NB launched this round enters service in 2037-2040, before a 2045 Open Fan. Against hold it runs -8.00 / -57.60 / -35.40 / -41.46 / -51.84 / -16.07. Its RISE premium would be $8.78B to $37.34B, above the $15B allowance in five of six columns. A 2030 launch is ready no earlier than a 2035 one. Lobby does nothing without a live Open Fan (-1.00 in every column). RISE stays whole as technology and is never cancelled for cost (H5). The one RISE allowance stays unused, kept for an airframer path [CX-0469, CX-0205]. MY 20% LINE: rebutted, not struck. The line binds the next-generation product, RISE [CX-0217]. Ali confirms a ducted engine gets less than half the open fan's gain [CX-0183, CX-0180], so it will not meet 20%. It is therefore offered and described only as a defensive engine under H3, never as our next generation, and the statement says so in words. Durability is not traded [CX-0208]: Ali raises no safety or durability flag; the Ducted carries no fuel-burn target to trade against; and durability holds the date, never the reverse. Gate reviews are cross-functional [CX-0012]. SAFRAN GATE (CFM parity rule): - Ducted: consent assumed. A defence that keeps an airframer on CFM fits joint practice in serving both airframers [CX-0185, CX-0587]. Safran shares 50-50 in the installed-base annuity at risk in S3. There is no price talk, and RISE, the joint next generation, is untouched. - Partner Embraer: consent assumed. A CFM engine for a third airframer serves every airframer and locks no one out. This is inference; there is no Embraer evidence. - Open Fan and Lobby: held, so nothing to gate. - GEnx: GE alone, no gate. - Any CFM price or terms: joint with Safran [CX-0184]. MONEY (Ghai): - New R&D and strain run $0.67B a year for the Ducted and $1.00B for the package, inside 2-3% of about $44B revenue ($0.88-1.32B). - Against about $2.55B of room after a 70%+ return of about $8.5B free cash flow [CX-0645], headroom is $1.55B. No debt, no rating effect. - Premium is $0.00 in S2 and on both sets of weights. SUPPLY (Ali): the package pays the $2B strain in S2-S5 (+1.21 to +3.65 over the Ducted alone). If the base can carry only one project, the Ducted goes alone. STANDING COMMITMENT FOR THE BOARD REVIEW: if Partner Embraer is vetoed, GEnx goes with it (-1.22 as the second project), leaving the Ducted alone. If the Ducted is vetoed, Embraer falls and I run GEnx upgrade alone (+0.78). DOCTRINE, NOT MY RECORD, drove Embraer, Lobby, GEnx as the third project, and the cancel path. My record never addresses Embraer or lobbying (profile §6; dashboard_game §2, §5). NEXT ROUND: I will look at the airframer launches and selections on the record. If no threat appears by 2035, a cancel writes off $3.33B to save $0.67B, so the decision is judged then on its own grid, never for RISE.

Weighing the CFO. I weighted Ghai heavily: his record says his profit calls land [CX-0910], and he ran every option column by column. His arithmetic confirmed mine: Ducted +10.17 in S2, +5.58 and +5.86 weighted, breakeven 0.687; package +10.61 against GEnx alone, breakeven 0.623; GEnx -1.22 as the second project; capex $1.00B a year against $2.55B of room, with no rating effect. I took all of his binding vetoes as guardrails, and none is ordered: no Open Fan, no Lobby, no GEnx beside a Ducted alone, no S1 expected column, and no Embraer without GEnx. His one failed test on the plan, volumes-first on Partner Embraer, I answered as he proposed. I declared its $0.00 S1 gap inside the package in premium and recorded it in overrides. I also took his guide-low advice and booked -50.41. His volume dates slip [CX-0987], and here the unverified volume is the airframer's. That is why the Ducted rests on the hard rule 3 trigger (S3), not on agreed volumes.

Weighing the operating head. Ali's memo is a thin record. His own words end in March 2024 and cover engineering only, and on supply and Embraer he says he is following doctrine and my description of his job [CX-0633]. So I took his date and physics tests as binding and checked his supply view against doctrine. Dates: the Ducted is ready in 2036 as a test-gated floor, the Open Fan not before 2045 whether launched in 2030 or 2035, and the statement gives no RISE demo date and no Ducted date before 2036. Safety: he raises no safety or durability flag, and gate calls go to a cross-functional team [CX-0012]; I set that up as a private move with Safran's engineers. Physics: he confirms the Ducted will not reach 20% [CX-0183, CX-0180], which lets me answer my red line by keeping the Ducted defensive and never calling it the next generation. He also warns that his demonstration dates slipped, so a one-year margin to 2037 is thin. A slip still earns from the ready year, so I accept the risk and keep 2036 a gate, not a promise. Supply: the package pays the $2B strain in S2-S5, and he would keep the Ducted alone if the base can carry only one project. That is my fallback too.

  • Keep the payout whole; state R&D and strain per year against the room after a 70% return; put every premium in dollars in premium. Taken up. Ducted $0.67B a year; package $1.00B a year including the strain. That is inside 2-3% of about $44B revenue ($0.88-1.32B) and leaves $1.55B of headroom on about $2.55B of room after returning at least 70% of about $8.5B free cash flow. No debt and no rating effect. premium is $0.00, reckoned in S2 and cross-checked on both sets of weights; the RISE allowance is $0.00.
  • Public statement: name no rival, blame no one, give no Open Fan entry before 2045 and no CFM price talk without Safran; tell the market what we know and what we don't. Taken up. The statement names no rival and blames no one. It gives no Open Fan date at all ('really not for us to say'), no RISE demo date, and no ducted date before 2036. It has no price or terms language and is framed as what we know and what we don't [CX-0436].

Objective. Dominate NB engines (at least 50% in 2040, 2045 and 2050): met today at 76%. My reading of the public rules (inference; the brief gives no share path by column): - The line is at risk from 2040 in S3 and S6 whatever we order. In those columns the new airframe's slot goes to others and the remaining CFM slot shrinks. - It may be close in S4 and S5. - The Ducted (+10 pp) and Embraer (+5 pp) are the only levers that push toward it, and both pay on the grid, so no objective premium is spent. Introduce the Open Fan (launched and ready by 2050): not met. - 2035 is the last launch that is ready by 2050. - If an NB launches this round, it enters service in 2037-2040, so even a 2035 Open Fan would wait. The 'introduce' goal may then have to be given up on the dashboard. - I will not stretch the airframer-path test or spend the RISE allowance to meet it. RISE stays whole as technology. Objective premium this round: $0.00.

Predictions. Column weights: S1 0.25, S2 0.30, S3 0.15, S4 0.05, S5 0.15, S6 0.10. Airframers: - Airbus is the more likely mover this round; an NGSA alone gains 3 pp a year. I expect a dual-source code like today's, with a single-source rival code as the low case. - Boeing is less likely to launch now. A 10-year fps or a launch alongside Airbus carries the rest. - All six columns are plausible. Engine makers: another maker may launch a new NB engine, or commit to a Joint Venture, if it is selected. A Joint Venture commitment (-10 pp to CFM) is in no column and is a risk I watch. On these weights: - Ducted against hold: +5.58. - Package against GEnx alone: +5.94. - Package against hold: +6.71. - Weighted package PV: -38.70. I book lower, at the equal-weight -50.41. Widebody: no re-engine expected this round, so the GEnx upgrade counts from 2042.

Expected ΔPV. −50.41 $B (board after the round: −31.20 $B)

Other moves.

  • RISE continues whole as technology, 50-50 with Safran (public): Ground and component testing continues, funded as technology with no program dividend [CX-0174, CX-0214]. It becomes a product only when an airframer wants it [CX-0469]. No fly-demo, ground-test, flight-test or entry date is given (Ali's date ground).
  • Cross-functional gate reviews on the ducted engine (private): Ready year, durability and safety-critical parts go to the one supply chain, engineering and quality organisation [CX-0633], with Safran's engineers on a CFM engine. No single person makes a safety call [CX-0012]. 2036 is reported each round as a test-gated floor, not a promise. If testing shows 2036 needs a durability shortcut, the date moves and the slip is reported as a flag; durability is never traded for the date [CX-0208].
  • Supplier readiness on the constrained base before the ducted development load lands (private): FLIGHT DECK work on the 9 suppliers and 15 sites behind 80% of shortages [CX-0613], so the ducted programme does not crowd out LEAP OE deliveries or spares [CX-0529]. Lean before capital [CX-0540, CX-0653].
  • Private airframer dialogue: every new narrowbody is offered a CFM engine (the LEAP derivative or the new ducted engine) (private): This goes to both airframers and to Embraer, and locks no one out (H1) [CX-0587, CX-0185]. Platform talks stay private [CX-0586]. Standard terms, with no launch-era pricing or concession. Any CFM narrowbody price or terms language is a joint decision with Safran [CX-0184].

Board guidance before the ExCo met

Priorities.

  • 1. Be on whichever new narrowbody launches, but don't carry an engine nobody has selected. The credibility objective (a new P&W engine in service on a new airframe by 2050) is NOT MET today. On the grid, Do Nothing loses -27.76 if NGSA launches without P&W (S2, S3, S5, S6) and -2.85 if fps launches (S4). The Board's preferred form is GTF2 Solo: launch if selected (sole source on a committed airframe, invest 'when we've seen it') [P-0746, P-0737, P-1347, P-1367].
  • 2. A return above the hurdle against Do Nothing and against a buyback. Each Board item's weighted value against hold must be >= 0 on the grid. The grid discounts at 10%, which is above the 8% of the 2017 intrinsic-value model. No premium should be needed this round [P-0731, P-0715, P-1165, PG-0024].
  • 3. Durability and readiness before entry into service, and the GTF fleet before a new engine. GTF2 launched in 2030 is ready in 2036. Every possible EIS is later: NGSA or fps 7-year in 2037, fps 10-year or via Embraer in 2040. Time on wing must come ahead of fuel burn [P-1360, P-1214, PG-0050].
  • 4. Keep the dividend whole and debt on its pre-ASR path. GTF2 costs about $0.33B a year, 5-6% of the roughly $6B self-funded envelope. No envelope stretch is needed this round, and the Board keeps its once-in-the-game stretch in reserve [P-0566, P-0686, P-0499, PX-0268].
  • 5. Commit to a Joint Venture with Rolls-Royce only on a public trigger, and then share risk, never the gear or core technology [P-1233, P-1875, PG-0047].

Expects to see. The Board expects these pieces in the package: (a) The grid row for the submitted orders, and the row with each Board item set back to hold. (b) Calio's expected scenario, his predictions over S1-S7 and premium. The Board expects premium = 0. If a shared code (6 or 7) could trigger GTF2, his rationale should declare the shared-source choice as doctrine relief. (c) From Mitchill: - his own S1-S7 probabilities; - each item's weighted value against hold; - for any unconditional launch, the edge over launch if selected, computed as 3.79 x P(S3+S6) - 2.00 x P(S1+S7); - the cancel round for an unselected 2030 launch (2035), with its write-off of $2B x 5/6 = $1.67B; - an envelope check ($0.33B a year against about $6B), with the dividend covered and the debt path intact; - his four veto grounds, each marked passed or failed. (d) From Eddy: GTF2 ready in 2036 against each live airframe's EIS (2037 or 2040); the durability programme (time on wing, not fuel burn alone); and a parts and capacity result showing that GTF fleet recovery comes first. Also his two veto checks. (e) Every red-line flag, with how the CEO struck or rebutted it. The overrides list must be empty. (f) The public_statement text. If a piece is missing, the Board will compute it from the brief and say so.

Would approve.

  • GTF2 Solo: launch if selected, on any weights. Its value against hold by column is S1 0, S2 +50.49, S3 0, S4 +22.16, S5 +49.76, S6 0, S7 0. It is never below hold, and it spends nothing unless an airframer names P&W this round (codes 2, 6 or 7). If triggered, GTF2 is ready in 2036, ahead of the earliest EIS in 2037. It passes Return hurdle, Bounded downside, Durability first and Dividend and envelope. Its value in the trigger columns is its own condition, not booked upside.
  • GTF2 Solo: launch (unconditional) only as NGSA franchise defence, and only if all of the following hold: - Mitchill's weights show 3.79 x P(S3+S6) - 2.00 x P(S1+S7) >= +0.50. That needs P(S3+S6) >= 0.43 if the rest of the weight sits in S1 and S7; break-even is 0.35. - The 2035 cancel test is named, with its write-off of $1.67B. - No Mitchill veto for carrying an unselected engine is left unresolved. - Eddy confirms readiness and durability. Its worst column against hold is -2.00 (S1, S7), which equals its own bill, so Bounded downside passes. Launch is identical to launch if selected in S2, S4 and S5, so its case can rest only on S3 and S6 (+3.79).
  • hold on GTF2 Solo or Joint Venture with RR. It is not a Board item and is never vetoed. A round in which every order is hold never reaches the Board.

Would veto.

  • Joint Venture with RR: commit, this round. It fails the Joint Venture conditions: no Rolls-Royce commitment is on the public record, and no airframe is live with code 1, 4, 5 or 7. Its value against hold is -2.00 in S7 and 0 elsewhere, so it is below 0 whenever S7 carries weight. No premium can carry it, because no live airframe's EIS exists for it to serve. Beside an unconditional launch its value is 0 in every column, but the trigger still fails. Acceptable alternative: hold.
  • GTF2 Solo: launch whose weighted edge over launch if selected is below +$0.50B, for example with weight concentrated in S1 or S7. It fails Committed airframe, since no selection of P&W is on the record in 2030. A premium cannot relax that test. Acceptable alternatives: launch if selected or hold.
  • Any Board item that carries an unresolved Mitchill veto (dividend or debt path, an unselected engine, aggressive terms, unproven upside) or Eddy veto (durability, parts and capacity), an unanswered red-line flag, or any entry in overrides.
  • Any item whose case books a selection, a Rolls-Royce commitment or partner money that is not on the public record. Any item Eddy fails on durability or readiness. Any premium that is undeclared, serves no objective or exceeds $0.5B. Any plan that strains the dividend.

Recommendations.

  • Miss a cycle: order GTF2 Solo: launch if selected this round. It is never worse than Do Nothing, and it gains +50.49 (S2), +22.16 (S4) and +49.76 (S5) if an airframer names P&W. It costs nothing otherwise and serves the 2050 credibility objective. It also keeps 'Capitalise on the GTF' (ΔPV >= 0) met in S1 and S7, where an unconditional launch would sit at -2.00.
  • If the ExCo weighs an unconditional launch to defend the A320neo franchise against an NGSA without P&W, show the Board the edge column by column against launch if selected. Only S3 and S6 (+3.79) and S1 and S7 (-2.00) differ. Show that the edge is at least +$0.50B, write the 2035 cancel test into the plan ($1.67B write-off if no airframe has named P&W), and record Mitchill's position on carrying an unselected engine.
  • Show the return against Do Nothing and against a buyback. Set premium to 0 unless a gap is declared with its reason; any gap must be at most $0.5B, must serve the objective and must stay inside the company's $1B cap. Money that does not clear the 10% grid is better spent buying back stock.
  • Hold the Joint Venture this round as a standing option. Bring it back in 2035 if Rolls-Royce commits publicly or an airframer lists code 1, 4, 5 or 7. Any Joint Venture must share risk and investment, never the gear or core technology. Rolls-Royce's own executives said a Joint Venture holds only while both partners are on the same new engine. With GTF2 live, a later commit should fold in GTF2's spend rather than add new R&D.
  • Durability before entry into service. Eddy's memo should show the GTF2 durability and time-on-wing programme and its 2036 ready year against each live EIS. It should also confirm that GTF fleet parts and recovery come first, so that the 2016-2023 entry-into-service problems are not repeated.
  • Keep the dividend and debt path whole. GTF2's roughly $0.33B a year fits the self-funded envelope of about $6B, so no stretch is needed; keep the one-round stretch for later in the game. Mitchill should confirm the dividend is covered and debt is on its pre-ASR path.
  • Disclosure. The public statement should offer GTF2 to any airframer that names P&W, ready six years after launch, which means no EIS before 2036. It should claim no durability not yet proven, say nothing on airframers' dates, and book no selection or Rolls-Royce commitment. If a shared code (6 or 7) can trigger GTF2, the CEO should declare the shared-source choice as doctrine relief in his rationale.

Chris Calio frames the round

Question. Control what you can control [PX-0020]. Nothing has launched and no selection is on the record. Airbus and Boeing will choose their engines in their own rounds; that part is not ours to control. What is ours: whether we can answer a selection the moment it comes, with a GTF2 that is durable and ready by the airframe's EIS, without carrying an engine nobody has selected and without touching the dividend. So the question for 2030 is this. Which GTF2 Solo order (hold, launch if selected or launch) and which Joint Venture with RR order (hold or commit) lets us take any NGSA or fps selection that names P&W this round? Each must pass the safety and durability constraint first [PX-0035], then Neil's payback and return gate, then the Board. Second question: is there a franchise-defence case for an unconditional launch against an NGSA that goes ahead without us? On this grid that is the only column set where launch beats launch if selected.

Situation. Public record, 2030: no programme launched; everyone is on today's products. The 737 MAX flies LEAP-1B and the A320neo flies GTF and LEAP. Observed NB engine share 2026-29 is CFM 76% / P&W 24% / RR 0%, with no change. No engine selections. No Rolls-Royce Joint Venture commitment on the record, and no live airframe with a Rolls-Royce code (1, 4, 5, 7). Our position (brief): ΔPV +0.00 if nobody moves (EV $110B, WACC 10%, 960 NB engines a year). Objective: Restore credibility is NOT MET (no new P&W engine on a new airframe). Capitalise on the GTF (ΔPV >= 0) is MET at +0.00. Timing (rules): a GTF2 launched in 2030 is ready in 2036. EIS for an airframe launched this round: NGSA or fps 7-year in 2037, fps 10-year or via Embraer in 2040. GTF2 clears every possible EIS this round; the tightest margin is one year, on NGSA and fps 7-year. A Joint Venture would form only if Rolls-Royce also commits, and would be ready 6 years after formation (2036 at the earliest). What the grid says (ΔPV $B, S1-S7): - hold: 0 / -27.76 / -27.76 / -2.85 / -27.76 / -27.76 / 0 - launch if selected: 0 / +22.73 / -27.76 / +19.31 / +22.00 / -27.76 / 0. Never below hold; +50.49 (S2), +22.16 (S4), +49.76 (S5). - launch: -2.00 / +22.73 / -23.97 / +19.31 / +22.00 / -23.97 / -2.00 - Any row + jv commit: identical except S7, where it costs -2.00 unless an unconditional GTF2 is live and folds in. The miss-a-cycle loss is large [PX-0071][P-1347]. An NGSA without P&W costs -27.76 under any order, and an unconditional launch claws back only +3.79 of that. Most of that column is decided by Airbus's selection, which we win with product and time on wing, not price [PX-0055]. Trigger codes for launch if selected this round are shared-source in the grid (S2 code 6, S4 code 7, S5 codes 7 and 6), so the sole-source doctrine [P-0746] needs a declared relief.

Options to test.

  • A. Default: GTF2 Solo hold, Joint Venture with RR hold. Row 0 / -27.76 / -27.76 / -2.85 / -27.76 / -27.76 / 0. The Board's comparator. It fails my miss-a-cycle test: it cannot answer a selection this round, and it gives up +50.49 in S2, +22.16 in S4 and +49.76 in S5.
  • B. My lean: GTF2 Solo launch if selected, Joint Venture with RR hold. Row 0 / +22.73 / -27.76 / +19.31 / +22.00 / -27.76 / 0. It weakly dominates hold and spends nothing unless code 2, 6 or 7 names us this round with GTF2 ready by EIS. Shared codes 6 and 7 are declared as doctrine relief, not a PV premium.
  • C. NGSA franchise-defence hedge: GTF2 Solo launch, Joint Venture with RR hold. Row -2.00 / +22.73 / -23.97 / +19.31 / +22.00 / -23.97 / -2.00. Against B, the difference is S1 -2.00, S3 +3.79, S6 +3.79, S7 -2.00, and 0 elsewhere. Edge = 3.79 x P(S3+S6) - 2.00 x P(S1+S7). Break-even is P(S3+S6) of about 0.35 (if the rest of the weight sits in S1 and S7). The Board wants +0.50, which needs about 0.43. The cancel is named for 2035 ($1.67B write-off). Not for fps alone.
  • D. B plus Joint Venture with RR commit. Same as B except S7 -2.00. For the record only: it fails the Joint Venture trigger, since no Rolls-Royce commitment is on the record and no code 1/4/5/7 is live. The Board would veto it.
  • E. C plus Joint Venture with RR commit. Identical to C in every column because the live GTF2 folds in. It adds no value this round, still fails the trigger, and publicly signals a Joint Venture before Rolls-Royce has moved. For the record only.

Red lines.

  • Safety and durability first [PX-0035][PX-0073]: no plan puts a P&W engine on an airframe before it is ready. GTF2 (2030 launch) must be ready, durability proven, by 2037 (NGSA, fps 7-year) or 2040 (fps 10-year, Embraer). Eddy's readiness and durability veto binds on me.
  • Fleet first [PX-0080]: GTF2 may not take pacing parts, MRO slots or engineering from GTF fleet recovery. Eddy's parts-and-capacity veto binds.
  • No new engine without a committed airframer: launch if selected is the form. An unconditional launch is allowed only as NGSA franchise defence, only if Mitchill's expected edge over launch if selected is >= 0 (his ground 2 binds; no premium buys a hedge that fails it). The Board also needs >= +$0.50B, and the 2035 cancel ($1.67B) must be written in. No hedge for fps alone; no launch for share alone [PX-0009][PX-0109][PX-0055].
  • Sole source [P-0746]: shared codes 6 and 7 are accepted only as declared doctrine relief (we aim to hold about 40% of the shared A320neo [PX-0058]; 40-50% of a shared platform [P-1292]).
  • Joint Venture: share risk and investment, never the gear or core technology [P-1233]. No commit this round: no Rolls-Royce commitment on the record and no live code 1/4/5/7 (on the Board's would-veto list).
  • Dividend first, then debt back to pre-ASR levels, then buybacks [PX-0081][P-0686][P-0669]. No dividend strain and no envelope stretch.
  • Value, not share [PX-0055][PX-0100]: no launch-style discount, concession or free upgrade in other_moves or the statement.
  • Never speak for an airframer's dates or rates [PX-0062]. Book no selection, Rolls-Royce commitment or partner money that is not on the public record (Mitchill's ground 4 and the Board's veto).
  • Premium: doctrine plus objective never above $1B; the Board passes at most $0.5B, declared and serving the objective. Expected premium this round: 0.
  • No widebody engine [PX-0027]. The overrides list stays empty; on a binding veto we revise once, within it.

Initial lean. My lean is Option B: GTF2 Solo launch if selected, Joint Venture with RR hold, premium 0. Why. On the grid, launch if selected is never below hold, and it answers any selection that names us this round, codes 2, 6 or 7 (S2, S4, S5 are worth +50.49, +22.16 and +49.76 against hold). It spends nothing otherwise, so Capitalise stays met in S1 and S7, and it is the only route this round to Restore credibility by 2050. It passes my tests: - Visible demand [PX-0109][PX-0009]: the commitment coincides with the selection. - Miss a cycle [PX-0071]: we can answer this round. - Durability: ready in 2036, ahead of every possible EIS, subject to Shane's check. - Dividend safe: about $0.33B a year if triggered. The shared-source triggers (codes 6 and 7) are declared as doctrine relief, not a PV premium. A shared NGSA is franchise defence; we already run at about 40% of a shared A320neo [PX-0058][P-1292]. The unconditional launch (C) is the one open question. It gains only in S3 and S6 (+3.79) and loses $2.00B in S1 and S7. It needs P(S3+S6) of about 0.35 to break even and about 0.43 for the Board. My own record says the next single-aisle comes "mid-next decade" [PX-0093]. That is my incrementalism bias, so I will not lean on it alone: the board gives Airbus a strong reason to move early, and I will take Neil's weights. Even so, P(S3+S6) would require Airbus to launch NGSA this round and to leave us off it. I do not expect that to clear 0.43. I will take C only if Neil's edge clears zero and the Board's +$0.50B, with the 2035 cancel written in. Joint Venture: hold. No Rolls-Royce commitment on the record and no live code 1/4/5/7. It is a standing option for 2035 on a public trigger, gear and core protected [P-1233]. My lean here is doctrine and inference; I have no record of my own on a Joint Venture. Proposed disclosure (public_statement): "The GTF fleet is still not where our customers need it to be, and fleet recovery keeps first call on our parts and our engineers. Control what you can control. Pratt & Whitney will launch its next-generation geared turbofan, GTF2, in any round in which an airframer names Pratt & Whitney on a new single-aisle. It will be ready six years from launch, so no earlier than 2036, with time on wing and durability proven before entry into service. We have learned our lesson from the prior iterations of the GTF. Standard terms; we are not in the launch phase on pricing. We will not speak for any airframer's plans or dates." Proposed other move (public, no board effect): continue the GTF durability kit for the installed fleet, sold, not given.

It books no selection or Rolls-Royce commitment, offers no discount, and says nothing on any airframer's dates or rates. I removed an unsupported fleet-state line on Eddy's flag. The shared-source relief is declared in the rationale at $0 PV.

Objective. Restore credibility is NOT MET. This round it becomes met only if an airframer names P&W (S2, S4, S5; p = 0.37 on these weights), and the order is the same under launch and launch if selected. If no trigger comes, a 2035 launch if selected is still in time: ready in 2041, in service before 2050. Capitalise on the GTF (ΔPV >= 0) is MET today. Under our orders it stays met in S1, S2, S4, S5 and S7. It fails in S3 and S6 (-27.76) under every order; that loss is Airbus's selection, not our choice. The unconditional launch would also have failed it in S1 and S7 (-2.00). PV given up for either objective: $0.

Predictions. S1 0.33, S2 0.20, S3 0.10, S4 0.05, S5 0.12, S6 0.08, S7 0.12 (sum 1.00). Expected column: S1. Aggregates: - Airbus launches NGSA this round: 0.50. - An NGSA without P&W (S3+S6): 0.18. - A P&W code this round (S2+S4+S5): 0.37. - Rolls-Royce commits to a Joint Venture (S7): 0.12. These are Mitchill's weights, adopted unchanged; my incrementalism bias would tilt toward S1. Expected PV by plan: - launch if selected / hold: +3.15 - launch / hold: +2.94 - launch if selected / commit: +2.91 - hold / hold: -14.02

Expected ΔPV. +3.15 $B (board after the round: −8.44 $B)

Other moves.

  • GTF durability kit (Hot Section) for the installed fleet (public): We keep offering the durability kit at shop visits. It is sold on standard terms, not given away [PX-0100][PX-0088][PX-0106]. We give no dated recovery of the AOG count; the brief has no 2030 count, and Eddy's dated recoveries and mine have slipped before [PX-0098][PX-0104]. It has no effect on the game board.
  • GTF2 readiness plan, held until a selection triggers it (private): We spend nothing on this until a selection. If launch if selected triggers, GTF2 is built as a derivative of the Advantage architecture, with the gear and core already matured and about 3x the testing reused [PX-0084]. Severe-environment testing starts early, all life-limited parts are at full life at EIS, and the six-year programme is not compressed. Eddy's ground-1 veto stands on any order or statement that dates GTF2 before 2036. Fleet recovery keeps first call on powder metal, castings and MRO slots [PX-0080].
  • Standing 2035 review (private): We write three tests into the plan. (1) Re-test GTF2 Solo: launch if selected against any airframe launched in 2030 or 2035; a 2035 trigger is ready in 2041, in time for any EIS of 2042 or later. (2) Test the Joint Venture trigger: Rolls-Royce's commitment on the public record, or a live airframe with code 1, 4, 5 or 7. A commit must share risk and investment, never the gear or core technology [P-1233], and a live GTF2's spend folds in. (3) Run a cancel test on any live GTF2 if an airframer drops P&W's code before EIS. The Board's once-in-the-game envelope stretch stays in reserve.
